newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin criticises former privatisation minister.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin criticises former privatisation minister.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Friday accused former Russian privatisation minister Alfred Kokh of mishandling recent sales of state assets.

"Such work will not do. The scandal around Svyazinvest and Norilsk Nickel is connected to the fact that some banks are likely to be closer to Kokh's soul," Yeltsin said in a televised interview. "But this will not do. Everything must be honest, open and legal."
Kokh resigned this week to pursue a career in private business, and Yeltsin accepted his resignation, expressing thanks for his work in office.
Kremlin sources linked Kokh's departure to recent auctions for a quarter of national telecoms company Svyazinvest and 51 percent of voting shares of metals producer Norilsk Nickel .

Uneximbank, one of Russia's most influential banks, won both auctions. The Norilsk auction was criticised for being unfair and providing for a low price and a winner known in advance, although the Svyazinvest sale was widely held to be fair by Russian standards.
